expected_approaches.summary: Expand a right boundary and shrink the left boundary while the positive-value window still reaches target.
key_invariants: For a fixed right boundary, repeated left shrinking finds the shortest qualifying window ending there.
Expanding cannot decrease the sum and shrinking cannot increase it.
tradeoffs: Relies on positivity; it is not a generic arbitrary-integer window technique.

alternative_approaches.summary: Build monotonic prefix sums and binary-search the earliest qualifying prefix for each endpoint.
alternative_approaches.applicability: Positive arrays when an O(n log n) alternative is acceptable.
assumptions: Positive values make prefix sums strictly increasing.
key_invariants: Prefix sum differences encode subarray sums.
tradeoffs: More storage and logarithmic searches than a sliding window.

reference_solutions.source_code: class Solution { public: int minSubArrayLen(int target,vector<int> nums){ int left=0,sum=0,best=INT_MAX; for(int right=0;right<(int)nums.size();right++){sum+=nums[right]; while(sum>=target){best=min(best,right-left+1);sum-=nums[left++];}} return best==INT_MAX?0:best; } };

class Solution { public int minSubArrayLen(int target,int[] nums){ int left=0,sum=0,best=Integer.MAX_VALUE; for(int right=0;right<nums.length;right++){sum+=nums[right]; while(sum>=target){best=Math.min(best,right-left+1);sum-=nums[left++];}} return best==Integer.MAX_VALUE?0:best; } }

invariants.diagnostic_goal: Positivity makes right expansion nondecreasing and left shrinking nonincreasing in sum.

complexity_expectations.diagnostic_goal: Each boundary advances at most n times despite the nested loop.

common_misconceptions.diagnostic_goal: Recognize that arbitrary negatives break the monotonic window argument.

failure_modes.diagnostic_goal: Continue shrinking while target remains satisfied.

edge_cases.diagnostic_goal: Return zero when no sum reaches target.

counterexamples.purpose: The best window appears after repeated left shrinking.
Shows why the positive-input monotonic proof cannot be reused unchanged.

constraint_mutations.diagnostic_goal: Test recognition that the standard shrinking argument no longer holds with negative values.

probe_opportunities.diagnostic_goal: Defend why a removed left value cannot help a shorter valid window ending at the same right boundary.
Test whether positivity is an essential assumption rather than incidental wording.

expected_good_signals: explains both expansion and shrinking monotonicity
weak_or_misconception_signals: claims the technique works for all integers
sample_phrasings: Which input guarantee lets you discard the left side safely?

weak_or_misconception_signals: multiplies the loops as n squared
sample_phrasings: Why does the inner loop not make this quadratic?

expected_good_signals: returns zero when best remains unset
sample_phrasings: What does your result represent if the target is never reached?

level_considerations.guidance: Expect an explicit response to the negative-value mutation.

reference_reasoning: The positive sliding window is the primary prior; other valid approaches should be judged independently against the stated guarantees.
